key_insight: Correcting only teacher-disfavored tokens in incorrect student rollouts improves visual mathematical reasoning without requiring figure descriptions at inference.
engineering_relevance: The approach addresses perceptual errors in smaller vision-language models without adding annotation or model calls at test time.
method: Collect on-policy student rollouts and separate correct from incorrect solutions.
Use training-only reference descriptions and verified solutions to score incorrect rollouts under a minimal-edit objective; apply corrective loss only to teacher-disfavored tokens.
Train correct rollouts with task-reward reinforcement learning rather than full-response imitation.
evidence_signal: Across model scales, the method meets or exceeds description-assisted base models, improves low-level geometric perception, and transfers to external mathematics and perception benchmarks.
watch_item: Training requires reference figure descriptions and verified solutions; a frozen same-size teacher remains effective but yields smaller gains than a larger teacher on most metrics.
paper_title: Edit, Don't Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
